title: Open-immersion and etale extension by zero have the same adjunction
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion], which is etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and let $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ be the category of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $T=U,X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $j_!$ be the extension by zero of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], the sheafification of the presheaf $j_{p!}F$, with the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] (unit $\eta_j$, counit $\varepsilon_j$), where $j^{-1}$ is the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Let $j^{\mathrm{et}}_!$ be the extension $v_!$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] for $v=j$, the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{s\in\Hom_X(V,U)}F(V,s)$, with the adjunction $j^{\mathrm{et}}_!\dashv j^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] (unit $\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_j$, counit $\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_j$), the adjunction used in [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map]. For $F\in\Mod(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $V\in X_{\Et}$ let $\iota_{F,V}:(j_{p!}F)(V)\to\bigoplus_{s\in\Hom_X(V,U)}F(V,s)$ be the inclusion of $F(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}U)$ as the unique summand when $V$ factors through $U$ by $\varphi$, and the zero map of zero modules otherwise, and let $\kappa_F:j_!F\to j^{\mathrm{et}}_!F$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $\iota_F$. Then $\kappa$ is a natural isomorphism $j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j^{\mathrm{et}}_!$ of functors $\Mod(U_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, and it identifies the two adjunctions: for $F\in\Mod(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $G\in\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $\alpha:F\to j^{-1}G$, the transpose of $\alpha$ under the adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] is the transpose of $\alpha$ under the adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] composed with $\kappa_F$. Equivalently $\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,F}=j^{-1}(\kappa_F)\circ\eta_{j,F}$ and $\varepsilon_{j,G}=\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,G}\circ\kappa_{j^{-1}G}$.

proof.text: In the recorded Lean constructions, both extensions are sheafToPresheaf followed by the same localization left Kan extension and presheafToSheaf [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The specified comparison is the right whiskering of the identity natural transformation by sheafification. Functor.whiskerRight_id therefore identifies it with the identity of openImmersionLowerShriek, so it is invertible.

Unfolding the two recorded adjunction definitions [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction, lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] gives the same sheafAdjunctionContinuous, transported by the same upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction. Their equality is reflexivity in Lean; no uniqueness-of-adjoints argument or new Hom bijection is needed.

Rewrite by the adjunction equality of Step 2 and the identity comparison of Step 1. The transpose equality is composition with an identity, proved by reflexivity. For the unit equality, the pullback functor maps the identity to the identity, and composition with the identity fixes the unit. The counit equality likewise reduces to left composition by the identity. These are the remaining three conjuncts, for arbitrary F, G and alpha.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NW-3327c2a0f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery. It is one commit with the item node and the report, and creates no new nodes. Sources checked: Stacks 03DI (sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero), including the summandwise construction alpha -> alpha' in its proof; Stacks 03S3 and equation-j-p-shriek; the main-20261015 proof of cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change ('degreewise isomorphisms'); and the blueprint proof of lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives. The cited statements give what each step takes from them. Step 1: the comparison iota/rho between the single-lift presheaf and the sum presheaf is correct, including a restriction from a V with no lift to a V' with a lift. Step 2: kappa and its inverse come from the universal property of sheafification only. Step 3: the presheaf Hom bijection is correct, and its naturality is exactly naturality on the morphisms of U_et. Step 4: the statement of lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives only says an adjunction exists, so 'its adjunction' has to mean the canonical one. That canonical construction (Stacks 03DI proof, the node's blueprint proof) is exactly what Steps 3-4 write out. Both adjunctions use the same j^{-1} and the same identification j^{-1}G(V,s)=G(V). I accept this reading, and the step says openly that the cited statement does not contain the transpose formula. Step 5 proves the transposes are equal (T_op = T_et kappa) through the universal property, not by abstract uniqueness of adjoints. Step 6 gets both unit and counit identities with the right domains and composition order. Edge cases checked: j = id, U empty, X empty, Lambda = 0, F = 0. The coefficients are an arbitrary commutative Lambda. There is no SGA, no cycle and no duplicate: a grep of the nodes citing the extension-by-zero and restriction-injectives nodes found none stating this comparison. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. No tool_uses, no changes.

lean.statement: theorem openImmersionToEtaleLowerShriek_adjunction_agreement (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] : IsIso (openImmersionToEtaleLowerShriek Λ j) ∧ (∀ (F : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) (α : F ⟶ (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).obj G), ((openImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).homEquiv F G).symm α = (openImmersionToEtaleLowerShriek Λ j).app F ≫ ((etaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j inferInstance).homEquiv F G).symm α) ∧ (∀ (F : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)), (etaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j inferInstance).unit.app F = (openImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).unit.app F ≫ (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).map ((openImmersionToEtaleLowerShriek Λ j).app F)) ∧ (∀ (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)), (openImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).counit.app G = (openImmersionToEtaleLowerShriek Λ j).app ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).obj G) ≫ (etaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j inferInstance).counit.app G)
lean.note: The specified comparison is the sheafification of the identity on the common presheaf left Kan extension used by BOTH recorded extensions; in its empty/singleton-lift descriptions this is exactly the single-summand inclusion. The theorem states invertibility, the transpose equality and both unit/counit identities for the recorded canonical adjunctions.
